prompt: A documentary field photograph on the surface of an airless moon. Subject: one whole NASA Valkyrie-class humanoid robot built as bare lab hardware, not a person and not a spacesuit: no helmet, no visor, no fabric, no padding, no human proportions. Its head is a squat black boxy sensor head with two small stereo camera lenses and a spinning laser scanner on top, set on a thin neck actuator. The torso is an open aluminium frame holding a grey battery pack and an exposed circuit box, black and copper cable harnesses zip-tied along it. Arms and legs are machined aluminium tubes and white composite covers with some covers missing, showing round silver rotary actuators at shoulder, elbow, hip and knee, linear ball-screw actuators along the shins and thighs, belts and bolt heads; knees slightly bent in a stiff robotic crouch, torso leaning forward over its work, feet wide. Its feet are flat rectangular aluminium plates with a black rubber sole. Task: both mechanical hands grip a long-handled sample rake, a metal pole with a wire-tined scoop basket at the end, dragged through the ground in front of it; the basket holds a few small rocks. Both feet are planted flat on the ground. Behind it a line of its own flat rectangular robot footprints, plain smooth rectangles pressed into the dust with no tread pattern, and in front of it the rake has combed a fresh striped strip in the regolith. No human footprints, no boot prints, no people: the only marks are the robot's and the rake's. Ground: grey lunar regolith, fine powdery dust, pebbles, a small crater rim behind. Light: one hard white sun from behind the camera, high on the right, about 45 degrees up, the sun itself OUTSIDE the frame; no sun disc, no bloom, no glow, no flare. The robot's shadow falls away from the camera up-frame to the upper left on the dust, one solid near-black sharp-edged figure showing the boxy head, the bent knees and the long rake pole, joining both feet at their contact. The shade side of the robot is clearly darker than the sun side; no fill light. Sky: a narrow strip of pure black at the top, no stars, no Earth, no atmosphere, horizon crisp.
